summary: rsync module is well-focused: T1 handshake to inventory modules (@RSYNCD greeting + #list — 'rsync_list' medium), then T2 per-module anonymous-access probe (opens fresh connection per module, requests it, reads @RSYNCD: OK vs AUTHREQD verdict — 'rsync_open' high). Stops at the verdict line — never transfers a file. Solid separation of enum vs proven-access. Biggest gap: no LIST directory listing to sample file names (elevate T2→T3 loot proof), no writable-module probe (require pushing a canary file to prove --read-only=false), no rsync-binary version detection for CVE-2024-12084 (heap OOB in checksum length handling).

findings.tier_evidence: @RSYNCD handshake completes and #list returns concrete share names/comments with no credential — an actual info-disclosure oracle, not just port-open.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed module names into known_hostnames when comments carry FQDNs; motivates rsync_open per-module probe (already implemented).
findings.tester_next_step: rsync rsync://IP:873/ — grep for backups, home, srv, web, www; each hit is a candidate for the next-step per-module probe.

findings.tier_evidence: Per-module probe actually received @RSYNCD: OK — a proven unauth session was granted at the protocol level (recce stops before transfer, but the primitive is demonstrated).
findings.promotion_notes: Elevate to T3 by issuing a --list-only walk + fetching a sample file (e.g. .htaccess, README) to prove read-loot. For write: attempt to STOR a canary; if success, T3 write foothold and often T4 RCE via web-root overlap.
findings.tester_next_step: rsync --list-only rsync://IP:873/<module>/ ; rsync -av rsync://IP:873/<module>/ loot/ ; also test write: echo probe > /tmp/x ; rsync -av /tmp/x rsync://IP:873/<module>/recce_probe ; and check for id_rsa, .git, backup.sql inside.
